link_notes: The paper is right, but the repo is DataSynthesizer, a different tool, and its README digest does not mention PrivBayes; the paper full text is also missing.

open_release.rationale: The paper presents PrivBayes as a differentially private method for releasing synthetic data.

quotes.text: P riv B ayes samples tuples from the approximate distribution to construct a synthetic dataset, and then releases the synthetic data.

pipeline_testing.rationale: Sources are thin; DataSynthesizer has a random mode but the digest does not show testing use.

ml_augmentation.rationale: Full text is missing and the abstract reports only accuracy, not ML utility.

statistical_replication.rationale: The abstract builds an approximation of the data distribution and reports accuracy against alternatives.

quotes.text: P riv B ayes first constructs a Bayesian network N , which (i) provides a succinct model of the correlations among the attributes in D

causal_inference.rationale: The Bayesian network models correlations, and nothing in the sources frames it causally.

education.rationale: The repo README offers demo notebooks, but they belong to DataSynthesizer rather than PrivBayes.

quotes.text: After installing DataSynthesizer and [Jupyter Notebook](https://jupyter.org/install), open and try the demos in `./notebooks/`

benchmarking.rationale: The abstract compares PrivBayes with existing solutions, but full text is missing so use as a baseline cannot be confirmed.

imbalance_correction.rationale: Full text is missing; the abstract does not mention imbalance.
